clue.text: A struggle to maintain one's faith

definitions.text: A struggle to maintain one's faith

parts.words: A struggle to maintain one's faith
parts.note: reads like a private battle against doubt, but means an armed conflict fought to uphold a religion

explanation.definitionFit: A crusade or jihad is armed conflict waged in the cause of a religion, literally a fight to keep a faith.

clue.text: Handle last watch astern

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word, watch, is wanted

parts.note: astern means at the back of a ship, aft

explanation.surface: A sailor clings to the stern rail during the final night watch.
explanation.definitionFit: The handle of a knife, axe or dagger is called its haft.

clue.text: Praise one in the Upper House in speech

indicators.note: in speech says the word is judged by how it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a member of the House of Lords, Britain's upper chamber, is a lord

explanation.surface: A peer is commended for a fine address in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in a non-rhotic British accent, where the R in the peer's title is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud is to praise highly, a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: A know-all appears perceptive over the port

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: a perceptive person is wise
Acre is a historic port in northern Israel

explanation.surface: Someone who claims to know everything seems shrewd about the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a person who affects to know it all, a smart alec.

clue.text: Dance and a drink to uplift a sailor

parts.note: rum is a drink, the traditional sailor's tot

indicators.note: in a down clue, uplift raises the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor

explanation.surface: A dance and a tot of rum would cheer up a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: A service attended by ancient head of Rugby

parts.note: the Royal Navy, RN, is one of the armed services
ancient means old

explanation.surface: A church service is attended by a former headmaster of Rugby School.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is a famous English public school; Thomas Arnold was its celebrated nineteenth-century headmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arnold was the reforming headmaster of Rugby School in the 1830s.

clue.text: Go back — but not to work

definitions.meaning: to withdraw or retreat to a previous place
to stop working at the end of a career, giving up employment

explanation.definitionFit: Retiring means both withdrawing backwards and leaving employment for good.

clue.text: A newspaper's deadlines?

parts.note: reads like the times by which copy must be filed, but splits as the paper's lines about the dead

explanation.definitionFit: Obituary columns are the lines a newspaper prints about people who have died.

clue.text: A terrible mess follows a meal

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
dinner is a meal

explanation.surface: Something awful happens straight after eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's dinner is a British idiom for something done badly, an utter mess.

clue.text: Game for two couples, but involving more of us

definitions.text: Game for two couples, but involving more of us

parts.words: Game for two couples, but involving more of us
parts.note: a round of golf or a match played by two pairs, a group of four people rather than just two

explanation.definitionFit: A golf or tennis match for two pairs of players is named for the four people taking part.

clue.text: A bit of a racket in pearls and horses

definitions.meaning: a tennis racket is strung with lengths of cord
a necklace of pearls threaded together
a stable of racehorses owned or trained by one person

explanation.definitionFit: A racket's cords, a pearl necklace and a trainer's stable of horses all share this name.

clue.text: Soldiers unable to withdraw

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, RE, are soldiers
unable means can't, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Troops find themselves unable to pull back.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw a statement or belief formally.

clue.text: Private drilling site

parts.note: reads like a privately owned oil well, but a private is a soldier and drilling is marching practice

explanation.definitionFit: A barracks square where soldiers are drilled and inspected is called by this name.

clue.text: Catastrophic changes to a musical

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the words after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disastrous rewrites are made to a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamitous and catastrophic both describe something causing disaster.

clue.text: Detains drunk and doesn't let go

parts.note: to detain someone is to hold them
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A police officer holds a drunkard and won't release him.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold tight is to grip firmly and refuse to let go.

clue.text: Make lay chap pro? Questionable

indicators.note: make tells the solver to construct a new word from the letters given

explanation.surface: A suggestion to turn an amateur into a professional is doubtful.
explanation.definitionFit: An apocryphal story is of doubtful authenticity, hence questionable.

clue.text: Service provider

parts.note: reads like an internet or utility company, but a church service is led by a cleric

explanation.definitionFit: A minister who conducts church services, a provider of divine service.

clue.text: Hurried from Grand Central

indicators.note: central picks the middle letters of the word next to it

explanation.surface: Someone dashed away from New York's Grand Central station.
explanation.definitionFit: Ran is the past tense of run, meaning hurried.

clue.text: He's been known to pot the white

definitions.text: He's been known to pot the white

parts.words: He's been known to pot the white
parts.note: reads like a snooker player sinking the cue ball, but pot means cook in a pot and the white is a white person

explanation.definitionFit: A person who eats human flesh might cook an explorer in a pot, as in old cartoons.

clue.text: Help I had with an article

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls receiving assistance together with a written piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Aid and help are synonyms, as noun or verb.

clue.text: Asian navies meet at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or muddled, signalling the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Fleets from different countries rendezvous on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vietnamese person comes from Vietnam, so is Asian.

clue.text: Stop sleeping and wash, having risen

parts.note: the wake is the wash left behind a moving boat
having risen means being up

explanation.surface: Get out of bed, have a wash and get up.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rousing from slumber and becoming conscious means ceasing to doze.

clue.text: Renting isn't a problem when difficult to move

indicators.note: problem suggests the letters are in difficulty, so jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Renting a home is no trouble for someone who refuses to relocate.
explanation.definitionFit: An intransigent person is unwilling to change position, stubbornly immovable.

clue.text: Assignment gets academic award

definitions.meaning: a ... of land or rights is an allocation, an assignment
money given to a student or researcher for study

explanation.definitionFit: A grant is both a formal assignment of property and a sum awarded for study.

clue.text: One to study a good figure

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
to con is an old word meaning to study or learn

explanation.surface: A student must examine a fine statue.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a revered figure, often a holy image of a saint.

clue.text: Fixed forms of worship

parts.note: reads like set liturgies, but forms are benches fixed in a place of worship

explanation.definitionFit: Church benches are long seats fixed to the floor, once called forms.

clue.text: Rise and go out for drunken binges

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Get up and go out for a night of heavy drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgies are wild parties of excessive drinking and indulgence.

clue.text: Hot food taken out

parts.note: reads like a takeaway meal, but describes food cooked and eaten outdoors

explanation.definitionFit: A grill meal cooked over charcoal in the open air is hot food eaten outside.

clue.text: Physical exercises I put off when on board

indicators.note: on board conventionally means placed inside S and S, a steamship

parts.note: board suggests a ship, SS being steamship

indicators.note: off means wrong, signalling the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone skips their gym routine while on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns I PUT into ITUP, which 'on board' puts inside SS, the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sit-ups are abdominal exercises done lying on the back and raising the torso.

clue.text: Special gifts of money

definitions.meaning: an ancient unit of weight and currency in Greece and the Near East

explanation.definitionFit: Talents are natural abilities and also, in the Bible, sums of money.
